discussion_comments.comment_body:
Fixed diagnostic precedence in `99546e2d07bff8cee10ef5476e0f991f0993f88f`: when startup and cleanup both fail, the startup kind/message remains primary and the cleanup failure is included.

A cleanup-only failure remains an explicit error. This bridge has no initialized tracing subscriber, and failed deletion can leave the registration behind, so tracing-only output would hide that failure. The bootstrap ACK confirms admission, not server readiness; the host checks readiness afterward.

Verified `DeleteTask` returning `E_ACCESSDENIED` in an owned ordinary same-account task probe, then restored its ACL and removed all probe resources. The error-priority regression and `just check` passed (3,514 Rust tests plus the other gates).

The compatibility gap is valid. I am adding a read-only check using the existing endpoint/capability/detached-server policy before either reuse return. Simply removing the returns would allow ensure_remote_server_ready to offer stopping an existing ordinary server, conflicting with the explicitly approved preserve-running-server behavior. Incompatible or disappeared servers will instead produce an error without stop/start side effects. Validation and the follow-up push are in progress.

Fixed in f4535c02. Both Ready and ordinary Conflict now query the running server and apply the existing endpoint/capability/detached-lifecycle policy before returning. Incompatible or disappeared servers fail without stopping or starting anything, preserving the approved existing-server behavior. Added regression coverage; just check passed 2,949 tests plus maintenance. Real SSH setup reused the same desktop PID and saved API access passed. The same commit also fixes a separately reproduced startup panic: FreeConsole left stale standard handles, so the startup banner failed with Access denied. Windows desktop detachment now clears them; native regression and eight consecutive full launch/TUI/API/cleanup runs passed.

I’m keeping the fail-closed behavior. Treating status 1 or 3 as confirmed is unsafe here: host pixel parsing is enabled only when the focused child requests 1016 and exact geometry exists, so an ordinary child would still route permanently pixel-valued reports through the cell path. Because this query follows an explicit reset, continuing cannot preserve consistent units.

Fixed in c199cd5e — confirmed and reproduced before fixing.

The timeout is now computed and validated before `stage()` runs, so no rejected request reaches the filesystem at all. Reordering was preferable to adding a `discard()` on this path: the timeout never depended on the composed command, so validating it first is where it belonged.

While reordering I found a second leak on the same stretch that the review did not flag — `terminals.get_mut(...).ok_or_else(TargetUnavailable)?` also sat between staging and sending. It is defensively unreachable (the same key succeeded on `get()` earlier with no intervening mutation), but a `?` that silently leaves a payload behind is worth closing, so it became a `let ... else` that discards first. Every path between staging and the send now cleans up.

Regression test added in `tests/long_command_delivery.rs::a_rejected_agent_start_leaves_no_staged_payload`. It is characterized, not just written — reverting the reorder makes it fail and name the leaked file:

```
a rejected request must not leave a staged payload:
[".../state/herdr-dev/staged-commands/agent-claude-4387-18d1cd818d366c78"]
```

Addressed in c199cd5e, though not the way suggested — the concern is real, the proposed remedy is disproportionate to it.

Reaching this requires an `XDG_STATE_HOME` of roughly 1000 characters, near `PATH_MAX` on Darwin. Restructuring staging around bounded relative references (the review labels it "Heavy lift", and agreed) is a lot of machinery for a configuration that is already close to unusable for other reasons.

What matters is not that pathological paths keep working, but that herdr never silently types a line it knows will be cut — that silence is the entire bug this PR exists to fix. So the rendered line is now checked against `MAX_TYPED_COMMAND` after composition; over it, the payload is removed and an `io::Error` is returned. `agent.start` surfaces that as `InputFailed` rather than reporting success on a command that never ran.

Five lines, and it converts the failure mode from silent truncation to a loud error, which is the property worth guaranteeing.

No regression test for the near-limit path: constructing one means a ~1000-character state directory in a temp dir, which is itself near the platform limit and would be fragile across CI runners. The invariant is enforced at the only place the line is built, and `the_typed_line_does_not_grow_with_the_command` already pins the property that keeps ordinary paths far below the cap.

Agreed, and fixed in 5bf4523c. The mechanism is exactly as you describe: the runner drops the late reply because the receiver is gone, then writes the queued bytes unchecked while the caller has already been told they landed.

My rationale for the fallback was wrong. I wrote it as "preserve the behaviour herdr had before this check existed", but that behaviour *is* the defect in #2862 — a success report for input the kernel truncated. Preserving it on the one path where we cannot answer defeats the contract the rest of the change establishes.

Every uncertain answer now refuses. A timeout returns a new `PtyWriteError::DisciplineUnknown` and the submission is never enqueued, so the caller gets a retryable error instead of a false success. I took the "return an error without enqueueing" option rather than holding the submission pending: keeping it pending would reintroduce the unbounded stall that was the first design's undoing.

I also raised `CANONICAL_VERDICT_TIMEOUT` from 100ms to 250ms. Expiry now costs a refusal rather than a silent write, so it is worth waiting well past a healthy answer to keep that refusal rare — the runner is a dedicated thread that normally replies within one poll pass, and the write gate is already closed during the handoff drain, the only place it stays away from its control channel for long.

Covered by `a_submission_is_refused_when_the_runner_cannot_report_its_discipline`, which drives a handle whose control channel is never serviced and asserts both the refusal and that nothing reached the write queue.

This was correct and is now resolved by removing the mechanism rather than tuning it. The branch was rebuilt as a single replacement commit (eb494b4c, plus 5bf4523c); `should_hold_canonical_submission`, the 750ms hold, the retry timer and the drop path no longer exist.

Your diagnosis was the decisive one. The hold ended in `discard_undeliverable_canonical_submission`, which popped the front submission and emitted a `warn!` — and `try_write_user_input` is fire-and-forget, so there was no path back to the caller. `agent start` had already returned `ok`. That made the end state of the fix a *silent loss*, which is the same defect #2862 reports ("the CLI reports success... a success-looking no-op"), with the truncated-fragment symptom traded for total loss plus a server log line. And as you noted, once the queue was emptied by the drop, a later handoff drained cleanly and reported success over destroyed input.

The submission is now refused before it is ever queued: the runner is asked whether the discipline installed right now would truncate it, and `PtyWriteError::LineExceedsCanonicalQueue` travels the error paths that already existed. `agent start` reports `agent_start_input_failed` and calls `clear_agent_name()`, so no phantom agent is left behind, and the caller can retry once the program takes over the terminal. Nothing is ever held, so nothing is ever dropped, and the handoff path is untouched by this change.

Correct, and no longer reachable: nothing is retained at all. The branch was rebuilt as a single replacement commit (eb494b4c, plus 5bf4523c) and `should_hold_canonical_submission` is gone along with the rest of the hold machinery.

Your case — a foreground program that deliberately stays in canonical mode waiting for a line — was the one the hold design could not serve. It had no bounded answer: retain forever and the pane is dead behind it, drop after a timeout and the input is destroyed silently (which is what the follow-up commit did, and what you flagged separately). Refusing at submit time is the answer that neither stalls the queue nor loses bytes: the write is never accepted, so no later write is blocked, every handoff still drains normally, and the caller learns immediately and can retry.

Worth noting for the record that the refusal is not a size test on the submission. It is a per-line measurement under the termios installed at that moment, so ordinary multi-line input larger than the queue is still delivered — `short_lined_input_larger_than_the_queue_is_accepted_while_canonical` pins that with 3000 bytes of short lines into a canonical, unread PTY.

Leaving this as-is. Physical OSC 4 reports contain only the palette index, not Herdr’s request ID. After pane death the client can still have the abandoned query active in its index-keyed tracker; allowing a fresh same-index query would let a delayed old report be attributed to the newer request. `Unavailable` deliberately fails closed for that client connection. Safe recovery would require a cancellation/acknowledgement protocol or retaining the orphan transaction, not just omitting this state transition.

`wait_until_stopped()` has no return value, so `stop_session()` returns success even if the server is still running after the timeout. then `src/cli.rs` prints `"stopped": true` unconditionally.

please make the stop wait return a result/bool and fail `herdr session stop <name>` if the session is still reachable after the timeout. the command should not exit 0 or claim `"stopped": true` unless the socket is actually stopped.
